mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO falls for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate below 4% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE remains below 4% for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related earnings and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where HOUST is below its 12-month moving average for three straight months.
